chunk_findings.detail: `_begin_run()` clears the process-global `_ACTIVE` list, but `_ReplyFile.__init__` appends every reply file to that same list. If a process can have more than one review in flight — e.g. an MCP worker handling a new `ddflow review` while a previously started background review is still running — the second review’s `_begin_run()` removes the first review’s `_ReplyFile` objects from `_ACTIVE`. If the first review is then killed by the background timeout, `_terminated_gate` calls `active_files(item, gate)`, which iterates an empty or foreign `_ACTIVE` and returns no files, so all chunks already checkpointed by the first review are not recorded. That reintroduces the “terminated by SIGTERM … nothing reviewed” failure the change is supposed to fix. The active-file list needs to be scoped to the individual run (or `_begin_run` must clear only that run’s entries), and it also needs synchronization if concurrent reviews in one process are possible.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/reviewers.py:_begin_run/_ACTIVE

chunk_findings.detail: `_assert_gone` treats any successful `os.kill(pid, 0)` as proof that the reviewer is still alive. That is wrong for a zombie process. In a container where the pytest process is PID 1 and does not reap orphaned children, the slow reviewer (`sleep`) can be terminated by the group SIGTERM, reparented to PID 1, and remain a zombie. The helper then waits the full 10 seconds, calls `os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)` (which has no effect on a zombie), and raises “the reviewer … outlived the terminated review”, failing a correct partial checkpoint. If the PID was instead recycled after the reviewer exited, the helper can SIGKILL an unrelated process.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_checkpoint_kill.py:92 `_assert_gone`

chunk_findings.detail: The generated shell script interpolates `pidfile` and `began` inside single quotes without escaping. If `tmp_path` contains a single quote, e.g. `TMPDIR=/tmp/o'brien`, the line becomes `echo $$ > '/tmp/o'brien/...'`, which is invalid shell syntax. The reviewer script then fails to create `began`, and the test fails with “the slow chunk never started” even though the production code may be correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_checkpoint_kill.py:44 `_setup`

chunk_findings.detail: The test directly spawns `ddflow` with `subprocess.Popen`, uses raw `os.killpg`, raw `os.environ`, and wall-clock sleeps to drive termination instead of going through subprocess/process/signal/clock ports or a fake. This violates [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies such as subprocess tools, clocks, and environment to go through adapters and says tests should use fakes instead of real subprocesses. The concrete consequence is a non-hermetic, platform-skipped regression test whose result depends on real process-group and signal-delivery behavior rather than the checkpointing logic.
chunk_findings.title: [r-adapters] tests/test_review_checkpoint_kill.py:71 `_kill_when_slow_chunk_starts`

chunk_findings.detail: `chunks()` promises “line-by-line” recovery so a torn trailing line does not discard earlier checkpointed chunks, but it actually decodes the whole file first with `self.path.read_text("utf-8")`. If the trailing torn line contains an incomplete multi-byte UTF-8 sequence—e.g. a reply with non-ASCII content was being written and the process was killed mid-character—`read_text` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is not caught by the surrounding `except OSError` nor by the later per-line `except (ValueError, ...)`. That exception propagates through `chunks()` and `active_files()`, so `_terminated_gate` loses the earlier complete JSONL chunks despite them being recoverable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/reviewers.py:chunks

chunk_findings.detail: The new `chunks()` method reads the checkpoint file directly with `self.path.read_text("utf-8")`, bypassing the required filesystem port in `ddflow/adapters`. This adds a new direct filesystem dependency in `reviewers.py`, so tests cannot substitute a fake filesystem implementation and this change no longer touches only its own files, contrary to r-adapters.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/reviewers.py:chunks [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test drives the real `ddflow` process via `subprocess.Popen`, and `_assert_gone` directly signals and inspects OS process state with `os.kill`/`os.killpg` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. Project rule [r-adapters] requires external dependencies and subprocess tools to go through a single adapter port and says tests should use a fake instead of the network or a subprocess. This test uses the real process/subprocess path, so it violates that guidance even though the violation is advisory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_checkpoint_kill.py:_kill_when_slow_chunk_starts

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_a_sigtermed_review_keeps_the_chunk_that_already_answered` uses `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(os.name != "posix", reason="signals are POSIX")`, but `os.name == "posix"` does not imply `sys.platform == "darwin"` or other specific environments where process group signals (`os.killpg`) behave differently, and more importantly, `conftest.py` provides fixtures such as `repo` that may expect specific test setup or isolation. However, more critically, `_setup` defines `cli.write_text` as a shell script using `#!/bin/sh` with command syntax (`#!/bin/sh
body=$(cat)
if echo "$body" | grep -q 'y_marker_zz'; then
  echo $$ > '{pidfile}' && touch '{began}' && exec sleep 120
fi
...`), which is not portable across systems where `/bin/sh` lacks support for these constructs or `grep` behaves differently, causing test failures on non-standard POSIX environments.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_test_review_checkpoint_kill.py:27

data.probe: REFUTED: EC.commit_at commits the immutable event log (the source of truth), committed at the merge door regardless of the git merge result ([log].commit_events_at includes merge); it is not uncommitted WORK to roll back with a refused merge. The rebased test test_merge_commits_the_primarys_uncommitted_shard_first asserts the landing PROCEEDS and the shard IS committed -- correct behavior, not a weakened assertion.

data.probe: REFUTED: committing the event shards at the merge door is always correct -- they are pending events that must land regardless of the git merge outcome, and the "worktree.merged" event is only appended (log.append) AFTER a successful merge. A refused git merge records its refusal separately (GM.record_merge "failed"); it never "commits uncommitted work" -- it commits only source-of-truth metadata.

data.probe: REFUTED: EC.commit_at commits the immutable event log (the source of truth), committed at the STATUTORY merge door regardless of the git merge outcome ([log].commit_events_at includes "merge"); its message is "events: merge {item}i.e. the event-log commit, not a branch landing. A refused git merge records its refusal separately (GM.record_merge "failed") and never leaves uncommitted CODE work committed -- only source-of-truth metadata that must land anyway. test (test_merge_commits_the_primarys_uncommitted_shard_first) asserts the shard IS committed and the landing proceeds.

chunk_findings.detail: `EC.commit_at` is called unconditionally before `W.merge` and is not rolled back if the merge is refused. Given the existing conflict-test state (base and branch conflict on `c.txt`) plus a dirty primary event shard, `EC.commit_at` commits that shard onto the base/main before the merge attempt; `W.merge` then still fails on the unrelated `c.txt` conflict, so the command returns `REFUSED` while the primary checkout has advanced to a new commit containing shard data (and a message naming the item, e.g. `merge T1`). The changed test removes the previous “HEAD unchanged after refusal” assertion and explicitly tolerates this HEAD move, so the new code intentionally leaves this non-atomic mutation of the primary base untested.

chunk_findings.detail: The unconditional `EC.commit_at(log, cfg, "merge", f"merge {item}")` is still not rolled back when `W.merge` returns `REFUSED` or raises. Concrete failure: primary repo has an uncommitted event shard and branch `T1` also changes both `c.txt` (conflicting with main) and that shard. The new line commits the dirty shard onto `main`, advancing `main`; `W.merge` then returns `REFUSED` on the `c.txt` conflict. The command reports a refused merge while the primary branch has still moved forward with a commit that may contain unrelated queued shard data. The modified test explicitly weakens the old invariant that a refused merge leaves `HEAD` unchanged and does not resolve the defect; it simply accepts the unwanted primary mutation.

chunk_findings.detail: `EC.commit_at(log, cfg, "merge", f"merge {item}")` is executed unconditionally on `main` before `W.merge` runs. If `W.merge` encounters a merge conflict (e.g., both the branch and `main` modify `c.txt`), the merge fails and returns `REFUSED`, but the unconditional commit has already altered the `main` branch's history by committing whatever uncommitted files (including unrelated event shards or dirty files from other concurrent work in the primary workspace) happened to be present in the primary repository at the time of the `merge` invocation. This silently pollutes `main` with unreviewed working directory state even when the merge operation itself is aborted.

data.probe: REFUTED (factual): EC.commit_at -> commit_shards commits ONLY the event-shard files (eventcommit.uncommitted_shards returns only .ddflow/events/*.jsonl entries; half-written shards are skipped, per the module docstring). It never stages arbitrary code/dirty files. A refused git merge commits only the immutable event log -- the door contract ([log].commit_events_at includes "merge") -- not "unreviewed working directory state". The merge refusal is recorded separately (GM.record_merge "failed"); main advances only by the event-log commit, which is correct.

chunk_findings.detail: `EC.commit_at` is called unconditionally before `W.merge` and is not rolled back if the merge is refused. Given the existing conflict-test state (base and branch conflict on `c.txt`) plus a dirty primary event shard, `EC.commit_at` commits that shard onto the base/main before the merge attempt; `W.merge` then still fails on the unrelated `c.txt` conflict, so the command returns `REFUSED` while the primary checkout has advanced to a new commit containing shard data (and a message naming the item, e.g. `merge T1`). The changed test removes the previous “HEAD unchanged after refusal” assertion and explicitly tolerates this HEAD move, so the new code intentionally leaves this non-atomic mutation of the primary base untested.
